description: Additional Medicare tax, excess Social Security withholding credit (multi-employer vs single-employer), and the over-withholding W-4 nudge.

cases.name: Additional Medicare Tax — MFJ under $250K combined
Excess SS withholding — multi-employer (refundable via Sched 3)
cases.rationale: Two W-2s, each with $7,440 SS tax on $120K wages. Combined SS withholding = $14,880. TY2025 maximum SS tax = 176100 × 0.062 = 10918.20 → $10,918. Excess = 14880 − 10918 = $3,962, claimable on Sched 3 Line 11. Engine checks each W-2 in isolation, so it finds no excess and misses the credit.
hints: engine.mjs: the `exSS` reducer checks each W-2 individually (`ss - round(min(ssw, ssBase) * 0.062)`)
the excess-SS credit is only valid when the taxpayer had multiple employers — it must sum withholding across W-2s and compare to the annual SS tax cap
fix sketch: `const totalSst = w2s.reduce((s,w) => s + p(w.sst), 0); const cap = Math.round(TY.ssBase * 0.062); const exSS = w2s.length > 1 ? Math.max(0, totalSst - cap) : 0;`

cases.name: Excess SS withholding — single employer does NOT qualify
cases.citation: IRS Pub 505 & Form 843 (single-employer over-withholding must be recovered from the employer, not via 1040)
cases.rationale: One employer withheld $7,000 SS tax on $100K wages (should be $6,200). This is the employer's error; the taxpayer can't claim it on 1040. Engine still credits $800.
hints: same fix as exss-multi-employer resolves this one: gate the credit on `w2s.length > 1`
